title: Christ the Prophet
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ the Prophet means that Jesus fully reveals God and speaks the final word of truth and salvation. He is the promised Prophet who makes God known and calls His people to hear and obey Him.
summary: Christ the Prophet means that Jesus fully reveals God and speaks the final word of truth and salvation. He is the promised Prophet who makes God known and calls His people to hear and obey Him.
christFocus: Jesus is not merely one messenger among many. He is the Son through whom God has spoken fully, revealing the Father, the kingdom, the Gospel, and the way of life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God promised a Prophet like Moses whom His people must hear. The New Testament identifies this promise with Christ, the One who speaks with divine authority.

Jesus reveals the Father perfectly. He does not speak from ignorance or speculation, but speaks what the Father gave Him to say. His words are spirit and life.

As Prophet, Christ exposes sin, proclaims good news, announces the kingdom, warns of judgment, and reveals the way of salvation. He comforts the humble and confronts the proud.

God commands His people to listen to His beloved Son. The prophetic ministry of Christ continues to govern the church through His Word by the Spirit.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often want a Jesus who comforts but does not command, or teaches but does not rule. Christ the Prophet speaks with authority over every belief, desire, and path.

This doctrine protects believers from false voices. The final and saving Word is not found in speculation, trends, or secret claims, but in the Son whom the Father has sent.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Listen to Christ as the Prophet God has given. Submit your beliefs, questions, decisions, and desires to His Word. Do not treat His teaching as optional counsel; receive it as truth that leads to life.
